items.label: stock bodily reaction
items.note: Find the specific physical detail this character would have.
items.positive: A shiver ran down her spine.

items.label: stock bodily reaction
items.note: The held breath is in nearly every manuscript; cut it or show the tension another way.
items.positive: She let out a breath she hadn't known she was holding.
items.negative: She let out a long breath.

items.label: stock bodily reaction
items.note: Name what the body does that this scene alone would cause.
items.negative: The heart of the town was its clock.

items.label: stock bodily reaction
items.note: Fear is more convincing as an action than as a temperature.
items.negative: The blood on the floor was cold.

items.label: named emotion
items.note: Naming the feeling stands in for dramatizing it.
items.positive: A wave of sadness washed over her.
items.negative: A wave of cold air came in.

items.label: named emotion
items.note: Say what is noticed, not the sense of it.
items.positive: She felt a sense of dread.
items.negative: She had a good sense of direction.

items.label: stock bodily reaction
items.note: Let the reader supply the tears.

items.label: stock description
items.note: Describe what the face actually does.
items.positive: The smile never reached her eyes.

items.label: purple stock word
items.note: Eyes are eyes.

items.label: stock description
items.note: Show the mischief in what the character does.

items.label: stock gesture
items.note: Show the decision as an act.

items.label: stock gesture
items.note: A stalling beat; cut it or replace it with a specific action.

items.label: stock gesture
items.note: A stalling beat; cut it or replace it with a specific action.
items.positive: He let out a deep sigh.

items.label: filter phrase
items.note: State the action; the compulsion is implied.

items.label: stock opening device
items.note: Describing a character through a mirror is a well-known shortcut.
items.positive: She stared at her reflection in the mirror.

items.label: intensifier
items.note: If the event is sudden, the sentence can be.

items.label: authorial intrusion
items.note: Foreshadow with an image, not an announcement.
items.positive: Little did she know what waited.

items.pattern: \bit was a dark and stormy night\b
items.label: famous cliché opening
items.note: Avoid even as a joke unless the story is a parody.
items.positive: It was a dark and stormy night.

items.label: cheating ending
items.note: A dream ending cancels the events the reader invested in.
items.positive: It was all just a dream.

items.label: stock phrase
items.note: Describe what fills the silence.

items.label: adverb-propped dialogue tag
items.note: Let the line carry the manner, or show it in a beat.
